Hi Ivy — great question, thank you. High level answers below; I followed up with engineering (cc'ed) for the technical caveats and a proposed exception template we can sign.

1) Time-to-First-Token (TTF):
- Non-streaming (single-response) endpoints: Redwood currently offers a P95 TTF < 250ms and P99 TTF < 450ms for models up to 70B on our hosted fleet (standard config).
- Streaming endpoints: because of long-lived connections and continuous token flush, our published target is generally P95 TTF < 350ms and P99 TTF < 700ms.

2) Sustained tokens/sec expectations:
- Streaming (per connection): we characterize baseline sustained output at ~20 tokens/sec per connection for conversational workloads, with short bursts up to ~60 tokens/sec depending on model and prompt pattern.
- Non-streaming: throughput is measured per-request; typical server-side generation throughput correlates to tokens/sec but is enforced via request concurrency and batching rather than a per-connection tokens/sec SLA.

3) Exceptions / trade-offs:
- For very large models (>70B), or when customers require extra safety filters / on-the-fly eval, we may relax streaming TTF and/or sustained tokens/sec commitments. Typical exception pattern: relax P99 TTF to up to 600ms and baseline sustained throughput to ~12 tokens/sec, paired with a service credit (or reserved capacity commitment) and an agreed fallback policy (automatic downgrade to a non-streaming endpoint if TTF degrades further).

I've attached a short proposal that formalizes that exception flow (SLA_Streaming_Exception_Proposal_v1.pdf) — engineering telemetry supporting the numbers is in the CSV as well. Jonas, can you confirm the numbers and whether there are additional constraints (GRPC vs HTTP/2, per-region differences)?

Next steps: if OrbitAnalytics is comfortable with a conditional streaming exception (TTF relaxed in defined scenarios in exchange for a credit or reserved capacity), I can draft the exception addendum and loop in LegalOps for signature.

Cheers,

Hi all — quick technical clarifications:
- The numbers Priyom quoted are consistent with recent telemetry from our hosted fleet in us-west-2 when using HTTP/2 streaming.
- For Dedicated deployments we can often hit lower TTFs (P95 ~200ms) because of pinned resources, but that assumes reserved capacity sizing is sufficient for peak concurrency. The exception pathway is therefore different: in Dedicated we more commonly offer capacity commitments rather than a credit.
- Private/on-prem: SLA terms are customer-specific; our typical position is to provide a performance baseline in the statement of work but not the same platform-backed uptime credits we give for Hosted.

On the credit: we usually offer a 10-20% service credit applied to the affected billing period for confirmed SLA failures under the exception addendum. Exact % depends on severity and whether the customer accepts a failover to a non-streaming endpoint during remediation.

If Orbit wants a deterministic test harness, we can run a 24-hour soak using their prompt set (we'll need sample prompts and concurrency profile). That result would be the basis for any formal credit calculation.
